record.title: Any-View Spine Plan
record.readme_summary: Plan: view translation, any-position detection, paired XR-CT gold prior (patent material)
record.date_evidence: Header chip 'SchwingNet · From 3D to X-ray · 21 October 2026'.
record.question: Can SchwingNet turn an X-ray in one position into another view, detect and classify vertebrae at any C-arm position, and use paired X-ray and CT sets as gold truth for the 3D prior, and what must the census count before each model is trained?
record.summary: A confidential (patent material, before the provisional) plan with three goals: a network that turns an X-ray in one position into another (AP to lateral), a detector and classifier that works at any position, and paired X-ray and CT sets as gold ground truth for the 3D prior. Its short answer grades them: paired X-ray and CT as gold truth is strong (registration-based labelling is near perfect in LevelCheck, 100% at 26 s, 99.3% at 7 s); any-position detection and classification is feasible with a measured gap (the project's own record on C-ArmLSpine: lateral naming 96.4% zero-shot from renders, AP naming 43.7% as a one-level counting error, detection 0.3% from renders alone, 80.5% with other devices' real frames, 84.0% with 24 frames of the device added); AP image to lateral image is hard as stated, since the closest published work (XraySyn) moves the view only 9 degrees, so the plan is structured transfer of the lateral's levels, corners and alignment from the AP, with pixel synthesis only as an auxiliary task. It tables the held paired sets (COBRA 692 cases and 375,618 projections, C-ArmLSpine 149 cases, DeepFluoro, Ljubljana, IPCAI 2025 not yet) and notes every one is lumbar or lumbosacral. Section 4 gives what the census (PR #76) must count per region with the estimated counts needed to test each approach; section 5 gives the order of work, census first, and says nothing appears in an external text before the provisional is filed.

key_claims.claim: Lateral naming transfers from 3D renders: 96.4% zero-shot on C-ArmLSpine with an encoder that saw the device only through renders, within a point of the 97.4% fine-tuned on the device.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: Naming, lateral, encoder that saw the device only through renders | 96.4% (595/617) | ... within a point of the 97.4% fine-tuned on the device.

key_claims.claim: AP naming zero-shot collapses to 43.7%, a one-level cranial shift that is a counting error, not an appearance error.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: Naming, AP, zero-shot | 43.7% | A one-level cranial shift: a counting error, not an appearance error.

key_claims.claim: Detection does not transfer from today's renders (0.3%); real frames from other devices carry most of it (80.5%), and 24 frames of the device take it to 84.0%.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: Detection from renders alone | 0.3% ... Detection with other devices' real frames plus renders | 80.5% ... Detection with 24 frames of the device added | 84.0%

key_claims.claim: No published work turns a spine AP film into a lateral one; the closest moves the view only 9 degrees, and AP to lateral is a 90 degree move.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: No published work turns a spine AP film into a lateral one. The closest work moves the view only 9 degrees.

key_claims.claim: A synthesised lateral is a display aid and must never be read as a film, since what an AP does not show a model cannot recover.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: A listhesis or a wedged body seen only on the lateral is invisible on the AP, and a synthesised lateral would paint the typical spine in its place.

key_claims.claim: Registration-based level labelling is near perfect: LevelCheck labelled 100% of views at about 26 s and 99.3% at 7 s, with sub-millimetre projection error.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: LevelCheck (Lo et al., Spine 2015, 20 thoracolumbar surgery patients, 10,000 perturbed views) labelled 100% of views correctly at about 26 s, and 99.3% at 7 s.

key_claims.claim: The project holds more real AP-lateral pairs than the report assumed: BUU-LSPINE's 3,600 people, on the scale of LatXGen's 2,611 training pairs.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: BUU-LSPINE is held: 3,600 people with an AP and a lateral lumbar film each, with end-plate lines. That is on the scale of LatXGen's 2,611 training pairs.

key_claims.claim: There are no real paired films above the lumbar spine among the held sets, so cervical and thoracic transfer rests on renders until pairs are found.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: There are no real paired films above the lumbar spine among the held sets.

key_claims.claim: Every held paired X-ray/CT set is lumbar or lumbosacral, so the prior's thoracic and cervical parts can be checked only on renders.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: every held paired set is lumbar or lumbosacral. The prior's thoracic and cervical parts can be checked only on renders until a paired set there is found.

key_claims.claim: SyntheX shows physics renders can carry detection (6.44 vs 6.46 mm, Dice 0.80 vs 0.79, better at 10k images) but not always (chest lesions 85% vs 94%), so the 0.3% may be the renderer's fault.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: So physics renders can carry detection, but not always. Your 0.3% may be the renderer's fault, which is what the physics renderer ablation (#69) tests.

key_claims.claim: About 100 test persons gives a 95% interval near plus or minus 6 points at 90% accuracy, which sets the per-region count needed to test.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: About 100 test persons gives a 95% interval near ±6 points at 90% accuracy.

key_claims.claim: The first steps need no census; the decision to train each model waits for the per-region counts.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: Nothing below needs the census to start ... The decision to train each model does wait for it, because the per-region counts ... decide where each model has enough real pairs

decisions.decision: The first steps (renders and data plumbing) start without the census; the decision to train each model waits for the per-region counts.
decisions.reason: The per-region counts decide where each model has enough real pairs to be tested at all.

decisions.decision: AP to lateral is done as structured transfer first (levels, corners, sagittal alignment scored against the real lateral), with pixel synthesis only as an auxiliary task; a generated lateral is never read as a film.
decisions.reason: No published work turns a spine AP film into a lateral; what an AP does not show a model cannot recover.

decisions.decision: C-ArmLSpine's test persons stay out of every training, and a person used to check the prior is never used to fit it; the split is by person.
decisions.reason: It is the test device; keeps the gold truth gold.

decisions.decision: The order of work: census on the grid (PR #76) first; then the counting prior (#57) and AP/oblique renders with anchors (#59); then COBRA projected labels and the per-angle curve (#60); then structured AP-to-lateral transfer on BUU-LSPINE and C-ArmLSpine pairs (#68); thoracic and cervical transfer only once pairs are found.
decisions.reason: The counting prior and renders lift AP naming before the talk; COBRA is the gold set for the lumbosacral spine.

decisions.decision: Results go on slides as results only; nothing appears in an external text before the provisional is filed.
COBRA's commercial use (CC BY-NC) is a lawyer's question, not decided here.

record.title: Gold Tier 3 CT
record.readme_summary: Every gold tier 3 CT as one dataset: the members, the anomaly statistics with Wilson intervals, the studies, the sixteen quality checks, a reader bench whose verdicts are saved in the page, and the SQLite store in the browser (the store itself is rebuilt, its folder README says how)
record.date_evidence: README: "the owner's ask of 2026-10-27 22:49 UTC, thread \"Finish scan import and tier counts\"), published on 2026-10-28"
record.question: Which CTs does the project count as gold tier 3, what do their masks say about anomalous spines (with Wilson intervals), how do they fare on sixteen quality checks, and what have readers confirmed?
record.summary: A private, confidential page that presents every gold tier 3 CT as one dataset, with one row per study (member, site, tier, mask facts, two column calls kept apart, anomaly class and status). It holds 1,557 whole ENHANCE.PET studies plus 17 VerSe series (provisional until the sacrum is seen) and 142 TotalSegmentator v3 subjects declared without rows. Anomaly classes come from the release's names and the ribs, with 95 percent Wilson intervals. Sixteen quality checks run over 1,597 published masks and three repaired ones. A reader bench of 191 studies saves verdicts in the page's own store, and a SQLite store opens in the browser. The README states that nothing yet moves verdicts into the store's qa_review table, so no study is reader confirmed.

key_claims.claim: 1,557 ENHANCE.PET studies are gold 3 and are whole studies; 37 lack C2 (silver 3) and 3 repaired masks stay gold 4.
Of 1,557 whole ENHANCE.PET studies, 1,406 are typical by the names (T12L5), a share of about 90 percent (Wilson 88.7 to 91.7 percent).
Variant classes by the masks: L6 below L5 with 12 rib pairs 50, four lumbar 28, eleven ribs 33, L6 with 13th rib 14, thirteen ribs 2, asymmetric 4 (131 in all).
No anomaly is reader confirmed yet: two masks agreeing is not a read of the CT, and verdicts are not yet moved into the store.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: Nothing yet moves them into the store's qa_review table, so no study is reader confirmed until that step is built.

key_claims.claim: The quality checks cannot show that an anomaly is in the patient; a lumbosacral question always needs the CT, and no check reads CT intensity or mask-to-CT match.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: They cannot show that an anomaly is in the patient: agreement of two masks is not a reader's read of the CT, and a lumbosacral question always needs the CT.

key_claims.claim: The build reproduces the source note's table of rib findings on unusual lumbar counts cell for cell (100 controls, 39 L4-above-sacrum, 67 L6 studies).
Person counts are bounds: Leipzig and Careggi carry no person id, so persons are an upper bound.
key_claims.evidence_in_artifact: Leipzig and Careggi carry no person id, so their persons are an upper bound.
